newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK C/A DEFICIT UP 27PCT YR/YR IN FEB- CBANK.
newsitem.headline: GREEK C/A DEFICIT UP 27PCT YR/YR IN FEB- CBANK.

text.p: Greece's foreign exchange reserves fell to $16.3 billion at the end of May from $19.7 billion in February, the Bank of Greece said on Thursday.
The country's current account deficit widened 27.5 percent year-on-year in February to $853 million versus $668 million in the same month a year earlier.

"The rise in the trade deficit is due to higher import expenditures, up by $162 million, of which $102 million reflect imports of fuels. Export revenues fell by $76 million against February 1996," it said.
Similarly, The trade deficit in the first two months of the year reached $3.184 billion and was due to a 7.9 percent rise in import expenditures and a 14.5 percent drop in export revenues.
Current account figures provided by the Bank of Greece
